name: La Friche la Belle de Mai
funding: Ville de Marseille, Ministère de la Culture, Région Sud, European Regional Development Fund; cooperative non-profit governance (SCIC).

name: Triangle-Astérides, centre d'art contemporain
funding: Ministère de la Culture (DRAC PACA), Ville de Marseille, Région Sud, Département des Bouches-du-Rhône; non-profit association.
watch: Non-profit contemporary art centre and residency within La Friche; founding member of Triangle Network.

name: Villa Arson
watch: Brutalist architectural masterpiece overlooking the Mediterranean; public national art school and contemporary art centre.

name: Frac Centre-Val de Loire
funding: Région Centre-Val de Loire, Ministère de la Culture (DRAC); public contemporary art collection.

name: Fondazione Morra Greco
funding: Regione Campania, Italian Ministry of Culture, Morra Greco Foundation; certified non-profit cultural foundation.
watch: Restored 16th-century Palazzo Caracciolo di Avellino in Naples' historic heart; zero commercial gallery speculation.

name: Madre · museo d'arte contemporanea Donnaregina
funding: Fondazione Donnaregina, funded by the Campania region.
records_note: No annual report; the foundation's transparency portal posts accounts 2019 to 2026 and names its board, while the site lists no sponsors or donors.

name: Culturgest
funding: Foundation of Caixa Geral de Depósitos (state bank).
records_note: It posts reports and audited accounts for 2004 to 2025, a yearly funder table with amounts for 2009 to 2025, and its named board.

name: Tabakalera (International Centre for Contemporary Culture)
funding: Public centre funded by Gipuzkoa council, San Sebastián city and the Basque government.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Former tobacco factory; no current tobacco funding found.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2020 to 2025 with income and spending tables, a 2024 budget and its named board, but no funder list.

name: Contemporary Art Centre (CAC / ŠMC)
funding: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania; public non-profit kunsthalle.
watch: Largest contemporary art space in the Baltic states; home to the Baltic Triennial; transparent public institution.

name: Kim? Contemporary Art Centre
funding: Latvian Ministry of Culture, State Culture Capital Foundation, Riga City Council, Altum and EU social-entrepreneurship co-financing; project supporters KRASO, Kokmuiža and Media Port.
watch: Absolut and Valmiermuiža from the first text are not on its homepage. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: Kim? names its two board members and posts its statutes, but no annual report, accounts or sponsor list; shows carry their own supporter credits.

name: EKKM (Contemporary Art Museum of Estonia)
funding: Cultural Endowment of Estonia (Eesti Kultuurkapital), Tallinn Culture and Sports Department; artist-governed cooperative non-profit.

name: Kunstnernes Hus
funding: Artist-owned foundation; about page names no funders.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2015 to 2024 with accounts, a named funder section and the board; filings for 2023 to 2025 are in the register.
